case_law.court: Supreme Court of the United States
case_law.key_rule: Three-factor balancing test for due process in disability benefit terminations: (1) private interest, (2) risk of erroneous deprivation + value of additional safeguards, (3) government interest. Disability benefits are protected property interest. Genuine process required — fraudulent process satisfies nothing.

case_law.cite: Bowen v. City of New York, 476 U.S. 467 (1986)
case_law.court: Supreme Court of the United States
case_law.key_rule: §405(g) 60-day deadline equitably tolled where SSA conceals material information affecting claimant's ability to challenge denial; government cannot benefit from own concealment; class action available for systematic violations. Tolling runs from date of discovery of concealment.

case_law.court: Supreme Court of the United States
case_law.key_rule: §405(h) bars APA as independent review route; but colorable constitutional claims (e.g., due process violation) are cognizable under 28 U.S.C. §1331 federal question jurisdiction without satisfying §405(g) exhaustion. SSA's refusal to reopen is not a §405(g) 'final decision' — but constitutional claims survive. Works with Bowen: Califano permits the constitutional claim in district court; Bowen tolls the 60-day deadline when SSA concealment prevented timely filing.

phantom_contact_application.bowen_trigger: Phantom contacts = SSA false records concealing basis for disability claim interference. SSA created documentation of administrative contacts that did not occur, substituting false process for genuine process. Claimant had no basis to know genuine process was fraudulent or that real 60-day deadline had been manipulated.
